headline: The diffuse 3sqrt(2) Gaussian obstruction is a strict global local maximizer against arbitrary small insertions of up to three mutually orthogonal uniform heavy rows; the exact orientation penalty is (57W-33w_max)/640 at worst.

explicit_dense_stress.finite_matrix: A_{m,ell}=C_{m,ell}^T B_* C_{m,ell}; CC^T=I; all physical matrix entries nonzero; nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}; all physical laws independent centered unit intervals

lower_bound_consequence: Choose ell_k->0 and m_k large with m_k ell_k->infinity; exact finite dense matrices have three distinguished leverage rows parametrically heavier than residual rows while density peaks tend to 3sqrt(2), so C_univ>=3sqrt(2).

partner_result_applied.actual_application: On the face (ell,ell,0), the partner theorem gives c12(u)>=81/640; hence for sufficiently small ell, sup_u ||p||_inf <=3sqrt(2)(1-81 ell^2/1280). Its completed unique-global-maximizer perturbation step is then applied to the three-coordinate signed H4 perturbation.

finite_fourier_dependency.actual_application: For ell_j<=1/2 and m>=2 every frame leverage is <=1/2, so Theorem F gives |phi(t)|<=min(1,(4pi)^(3/2)|t|^(-3/2)); this upgrades the finite bank CLT to uniform output-density convergence.

proof_core: Variance matching cancels the linear leverage perturbation: h_ell=gamma[1-(ell^2/20)H4]+O(ell^3).
The product remainder is O(rW)(1+|y|)^(-8), whose quadratic pushforward is uniformly bounded over output level and orientation.
The isotropic baseline p0 has a unique global maximum at zero, so the partner global-mode perturbation argument moves the global supremum to the cone coefficient at second order.
Normalized Gaussian cone moments give J_{u,j}(0)/p0(0)=(57+6x_j-39x_j^2)/32, x_j=u_j^2.
The weighted coefficient is concave on the x-simplex, so its exact minimum is at a vertex corresponding to the largest heavy leverage.
constraint_on_sharp_proof: A near-extremizer analysis cannot exclude a few rows that are parametrically heavier than the diffuse remainder merely from scale separation; such exact dense finite frames still approach 3sqrt(2). But any fixed sufficiently small orthogonal heavy insertion lowers the global peak quadratically, with exact orientation penalty above.
unresolved: Intermediate leverage, non-orthogonal/shared-coordinate heavy rows, and finite or mesoscopic non-Gaussian residual components remain possible mechanisms for an overshoot above 3sqrt(2). Full universal upper bound remains open.
